title: The uses of boredom
text: For a long time, boredom was dismissed as a trivial [[1]], unworthy of serious [[2]] attention. That view has changed [[3]] over the past decade. Researchers now suggest that boredom acts as a signal, prompting us to abandon activities that have become [[4]] and to look for more rewarding ones. In a typical experiment, volunteers spend twenty minutes sorting paper clips by size and are then asked to solve a design problem; they often come up with more [[5]] solutions than those who skipped the dull task. Yet the effects of boredom are not [[6]] positive. When it becomes chronic, it is linked to poor concentration and even risky behaviour, and people who feel it constantly tend to report deep [[7]] with their lives. The challenge, it seems, is not to eliminate boredom [[8]], but to learn to listen to what it is telling us.

explanation.en: After 'a trivial' we need a countable noun: 'annoyance'.
explanation.cs: Po členu a přídavném jménu 'a trivial' následuje podstatné jméno: annoyance = otrava, nepříjemnost.

explanation.en: 'Serious ... attention' needs an adjective before the noun: 'scientific'.
explanation.cs: Před podstatným jménem 'attention' je třeba přídavné jméno: scientific (vědecký).

explanation.en: An adverb modifies the verb 'has changed': 'dramatically'. Two steps are needed: drama, dramatic, dramatically.
explanation.cs: Sloveso 'has changed' rozvíjí příslovce. Dva kroky: drama, dramatic, dramatically (u -ic přidáváme -ally).

explanation.en: We abandon activities and look for 'more rewarding ones', so the activities have lost their point: 'meaningless'. 'Meaningful' fits the grammar but contradicts the logic.
explanation.cs: Opouštíme činnosti, které ztratily smysl, a hledáme 'more rewarding ones', proto meaningless. Meaningful by gramaticky sedělo, ale ne významově.

explanation.en: An adjective is needed before 'solutions', with the meaning 'creative': 'imaginative'. 'Imaginary' means 'not real', which makes no sense here.
explanation.cs: Imaginative = nápaditý, tvořivý. Pozor na past: imaginary znamená smyšlený, neskutečný.

explanation.en: An adverb is needed before the adjective 'positive': 'not uniformly positive' means 'not positive in every case', which leads into the negative effects that follow.
explanation.cs: Příslovce před přídavným jménem: uniformly = jednotně, ve všech případech. 'Not uniformly positive' = ne vždy kladné.

explanation.en: After 'report deep' a noun is needed, and the context of chronic boredom and risky behaviour requires a negative meaning: 'dissatisfaction'. Two changes: the prefix dis- and the suffix -faction.
explanation.cs: Po 'report deep' je podstatné jméno a kontext je záporný (chronická nuda), proto dis- + satisfaction = dissatisfaction (nespokojenost). Pozor na dvě s.

explanation.en: An adverb modifies 'eliminate boredom': 'entirely', meaning completely.
explanation.cs: Příslovce rozvíjí sloveso 'eliminate': entirely = úplně, zcela.
